registered_before: any whole-normal burden of the levers below (campaign-interval rates of the joint_p CUSUM grid on pulse-live-recalibrated and pulse-stable-refreshed were already seen in ideas-screen-blind.json; nothing else)
goal: Lower idle-control positives, normal alert burden and false positives as far as possible without leaving the registered expectations (owner request 22/10: as few as possible).
scope: Pulse ML and its alert pipeline only. No rule-based signal (Falco, tripwire A1, declared exec probes from pod specs) gates, filters or overrides an ML decision (owner decision 22/10).
reference: stable candidate of 5.19: base29 (4bad16dc...), refreshed calibration (calibration-r6-1300-1900.npz), CUSUM on -ln joint_p, drift 3, threshold 6

levers.L1_cusum_grid: CUSUM on -ln joint_p, drift b in {2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5, 6}, threshold h in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12}
levers.L2_both_branches: p_and = max(tree_p, support_p) (both branches must be unusual; a valid p-value), with CUSUM on -ln p_and (same b x h grid) and with k2of2 at alpha x {1, 3, 5, 10, 20}
levers.L3_launch_conditional_calibration: Mondrian conformal by launch class: a window is in the launch class when execve or execveat is > 0 in any of the 4 windows of its context (current + 3 previous of the same container, contiguous as in the model); tree and support p-values are computed against calibration windows of the same workload and class (refreshed calibration span, 19/10 13:00-19:00 of pulse-live-recalibrated); a class with < 1200 calibration windows falls back to the workload; combined with the L1 and L2 rules
levers.L4_incident_grouping: descriptive, not selected on: episodes of one container merged into one incident when < G apart, G in {60 s, 300 s}; reported as incidents per replica-hour for every candidate (an attack in an open incident is appended to it, so detection is unchanged; time to human attention is not measured)

data.test: the next live run (confirmation run of 5.19 step 4, fresh campaign), blind: candidates are chosen and frozen before it starts
data.windows: one window table per run (scores, as-run p-values, exec counts of the context) built once from decisions + features; campaign spans (first interval - 60 s to end + 60 s) excluded from normal

metrics: p50 / p95 first alarm window_end - kernel event
selection_rule: 1. Feasible on a development run: recall >= 95 %, precision >= 95 %, idle control <= 5 %, p95 <= the tier.
2. Tiers: < 2 s (preferred) and <= 3 s (acceptable); one choice per tier.
3. Among candidates feasible on BOTH development runs, choose the lowest max-over-runs normal burden; within 5 % of it, the lower max control, then the simpler lever (L1 < L2 < L3).
4. A choice is proposed only if its burden is <= 0.9 x the reference's on both development runs; otherwise the reference stays.

5. Blind test on the next live run: a proposed choice is adopted only if it is feasible there and its burden is <= 0.9 x the reference's on the same data. Adoption changes the stable policy only after one more live run.
stated_in_advance: tighter rules trade latency for fewer alarms (seen on the campaign grid): the <= 3 s tier is expected to allow a lower burden than the < 2 s tier
L3 can lower recall for attacks that look like an ordinary launch; recall is checked per scenario
no lever is expected to reach 0.1 episodes per replica-hour
code: sentinel_pulse/attack/window_table.py (table builder), scripts/analysis/burden_levers.py (levers, metrics, selection); tests in tests/test_burden_levers.py
